# `sngl tool cgogen` wraps a package of the program's own as it does a
# library package: it writes the Go package wrapping the package's C
# declarations into cgo/ beside it, in the program's Go module, and marks each
# declaration with its wrapper, which a //go:generate line keeps in step. A
# function taking a ref is wrapped copy-in, copy-out, a C struct with fields
# among what it fills too; the struct is a Go type of the wrapper package's,
# named so from its first generation, before a mark names it. Each handle the
# package declares is a type of the wrapper package's too, crossing a wrapped
# function or not, so a program holding one names no cgo type of its own. Two
# declarations of one C function keeping a static callback are two wrappers,
# each keeping its own function, which C calls after both were kept. The Go program calls the wrapper, reaching the program's module through its
# own, which replaces the host module with its root (codegen.WriteGoMod), and
# compiles none of the package's C, which the wrapper package does. A string
# C hands over (#[c.frees]) is freed in the wrapper, through the function its
# preamble defines, as a member of a C struct is read and called (`field`).

# The program's module, which requires sngl from this checkout.
exec sh -c 'root="${SNGL_HOST_GO_MOD%/go.mod}"; sed "s|^module .*|module example.com/app|" "$root/go.mod" > go.mod; printf "\nreplace duckfam.us/sngl => %s\n" "$root" >> go.mod; cp "$root/go.sum" go.sum'
env SNGL_HOST_GO_MOD=$WORK/go.mod

sngl tool cgogen mathx
exists mathx/cgo/wrappers.go
exists mathx/cgo/split.c
grep '#\[go.native\("example.com/app/mathx/cgo", "cgo.SplitAdd"\)\]' mathx/mathx.sngl
grep 'func SplitAdd\(a int, b int, carry int\) SplitAddResult' mathx/cgo/wrappers.go
grep 'func SplitSwap\(p Pair\) Pair' mathx/cgo/wrappers.go
grep 'snglFree_split_free' mathx/cgo/wrappers.go
grep 'func SplitThingTwice\(t Thing, n int\) int' mathx/cgo/wrappers.go
grep '#\[go.native\("example.com/app/mathx/cgo", "cgo.State"\)\]' mathx/mathx.sngl

# A second run, reading the marks the first wrote, changes nothing.
cp mathx/mathx.sngl marked.sngl
cp mathx/cgo/wrappers.go wrappers.first
sngl tool cgogen mathx
cmp mathx/mathx.sngl marked.sngl
cmp mathx/cgo/wrappers.go wrappers.first

sngl generate --lang go --platform bubbletea -o out app.sngl
grep 'SplitAdd__result\(cgo\.SplitAdd\(7, 8, carry\)\)' out/model.go
! grep 'import "C"' out/model.go
! grep 'C\.split_state' out/model.go

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +6 tests, 0 failures'

-- mathx/split.h --
int split_add(int a, int b, int *carry);

typedef struct {
	int lo, hi;
} split_pair;

void split_swap(split_pair *p);

typedef struct split_state split_state;

typedef int (*split_fn)(int);

// Keeps f, answering where; split_call calls what is kept there.
int split_keep(split_fn f);
int split_call(int at, int x);

// A name for n, which split_free frees; split_fill stores one in *out.
char *split_name(int n);
void split_fill(int n, char **out);
void split_free(void *p);

// What split_free freed, counted.
int split_freed(void);

// A struct a program reads the members of, and calls one of.
typedef struct split_thing {
	int code;
	int (*twice)(int n);
} split_thing;

split_thing *split_thing_new(int code);
-- mathx/split.c --
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

#include "split.h"

int split_add(int a, int b, int *carry) {
	int s = a + b;
	*carry = s / 10;
	return s % 10;
}

static split_fn kept[2];
static int nkept;

int split_keep(split_fn f) {
	kept[nkept] = f;
	return nkept++;
}

int split_call(int at, int x) {
	return kept[at](x);
}

static int freed;

char *split_name(int n) {
	char *s = malloc(8);
	snprintf(s, 8, "n%d", n);
	return s;
}

void split_fill(int n, char **out) {
	*out = split_name(n);
}

void split_free(void *p) {
	freed++;
	free(p);
}

int split_freed(void) {
	return freed;
}

static int split_twice(int n) {
	return n * 2;
}

split_thing *split_thing_new(int code) {
	static split_thing t;
	t = (split_thing){code, split_twice};
	return &t;
}

void split_swap(split_pair *p) {
	int lo = p->lo;
	p->lo = p->hi;
	p->hi = lo;
}
-- mathx/mathx.sngl --
import c "sngl:x/c"

c.link(include="split.h", sources=["split.c", "split.h"])

#[c.native("split_add")]
func splitAdd(a int, b int, carry ref[int]) int

#[c.native("split_pair")]
struct _Pair {
    lo int
    hi int
}

#[c.native("split_swap")]
func _swap(p ref[_Pair])

func swapped(lo int, hi int) int {
    var p = _Pair{lo=lo, hi=hi}
    _swap(&p)
    return p.lo * 10 + p.hi
}

#[c.native("split_keep")]
func _keepDoubled(#[c.type("split_fn")] #[c.static] f func(x int) int) int

#[c.native("split_keep")]
func _keepTripled(#[c.type("split_fn")] #[c.static] f func(x int) int) int

#[c.native("split_call")]
func _call(at int, x int) int

func _doubled(x int) => x * 2

func _tripled(x int) => x * 3

func applied() string {
    var d = _keepDoubled(_doubled)
    var t = _keepTripled(_tripled)
    return "{_call(d, 3)} {_call(t, 3)}"
}

// A handle no wrapped function crosses.
#[c.native("split_state *")]
struct _State {}

func stateless() bool {
    var s option[_State] = null
    return s == null
}
#[c.native("split_name")]
#[c.frees("split_free")]
func _name(n int) string

#[c.native("split_fill")]
func _fill(n int, #[c.frees("split_free")] out ref[string])

#[c.native("split_freed")]
func _freed() int

func names() string {
    var s = ""
    _fill(4, &s)
    return "{_name(3)} {s}"
}

func freed() => _freed()

#[c.native("split_thing *")]
struct _Thing {}

#[c.native("split_thing_new")]
func _thingNew(code int) _Thing

#[c.native("split_thing.code", field)]
func _code(t _Thing) int

#[c.native("split_thing.twice", field)]
func _twice(t _Thing, n int) int

func members() int {
    var t = _thingNew(7)
    return _code(t) * 100 + _twice(t, 21)
}
-- mathx/gen.go --
package mathx

//go:generate sngl tool cgogen .
-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import test "sngl:test"
import m "./mathx"

func digits() string {
    var carry = 0
    var d = m.splitAdd(7, 8, &carry)
    return "{carry}{d}"
}

ui.window(title="t") {
    ui.text("{digits()}")
}

func testItSplits(t test.Test) {
    t.assert(digits() == "15")
}

func testItSwaps(t test.Test) {
    t.assert(m.swapped(1, 2) == 21)
}

func testItAppliesEach(t test.Test) {
    t.assert(m.applied() == "6 9")
}

func testItHoldsNoState(t test.Test) {
    t.assert(m.stateless())
}

func testItReadsAndCallsMembers(t test.Test) {
    t.assert(m.members() == 742)
}

func testItFreesWhatCHandsOver(t test.Test) {
    t.assert(m.names() == "n3 n4")
    t.assert(m.freed() == 2)
}
